full_judgment: Nazmun Ara Sultana, J. This Civil Appeal, by leave, at the instance of Bangladesh represented. By the Secretary, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare and others, is directed against the judgment and order dated 18.09.2014 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 1337 of 2014 making the rule absolute. Bangladesh Private Medical College Association (respondent herein) filed the above mentioned writ petition challenging the increase of the minimum "cut-off" mark from 110 to 120 out of total 200 marks for admission to M.B.B.S. course for the session 2013-2014 communicated by memo No. Sha: ODhi/Chi: Shi:/Borti/MBBS/2013-2014/204 dated 05.11.2013 issued by the respondent No. 4 (Annexure-A-1 to the writ petition). The case of the writ petitioner, in short, is that the writ-petitioner association is comprised of members representing private medical colleges of Bangladesh. The primary responsibilities of the writ-petitioner is to ensure, amongst others, that all the private medical colleges maintain an enhanced standard of education for their students, which will enable them to acquire all the necessary academic and practical medical experiences before obtaining the M.B.B.S. decree. That the respondents No. 1 (Secretary Ministry of Health and Family Welfare) framed a guidelines for admission of students in M.B.B.S/B.D.S. courses (the Nitimala, 2011) stipulating qualification criteria for admission of students in the B.B.B.S/B.D.S. courses in all Medical/Dental Colleges (public/private) in Bangladesh. Clause 22 of that Nitimala, 2011 states, inter-alia, that an application must acquire a combined grade point average (G.P.A.) of minimum 8.00 in his/her respective S.S.C. and H.S.C. examinations from the Science Faculty provided he/she does not carry less than G.P.A. 3.50 in any of the aforesaid examinations. The respondent No. 1 by an office order being No. ShaKomo/Chishi-1/Be: Me: Co: cha: Borti-01/2011/843 dated 04.12.2012 stipulated, amongst others, the admission criteria for the M.B.B.S/B.D.S. courses for the session 2012-2013 according to which an applicant is required to have merit score of 110 for being eligible to get admission to the M.B.B.S. course. That to the Knowledge of the writ-petitioner the aforesaid office order dated 04.12.2012 was not amended, neither the respondent No. 1 nor the respondent No. 2 (Director General, Directorate of Health Services) informed the writ-petitioner or its members of any such change. That in the notice dated 27.08.2013 issued by the respondent No. 2 inviting applicant for admission to M.B.B.S. course for the session 2013-2014 there was no mention that the applicants should have minimum merit score of 120 for being eligible for admission. But the respondent No. 1 in its meeting dated 23.09.2013 recommended that in order to be eligible for admission an applicant must have a minimum "cut-off" marks of 120 out of total marks of 200 for his/her admission to M.B.B.S. course for the session 2013-2014 and thus introduced a new minimum qualification criteria for admission raising the "cut-off" mark from 110 to 120. The writ Petitioner has stated that considerable number of seat in private medical/dental colleges for the session 2013-2014 are still vacant after the admission of students to the M.B.B.S. course due to this increase of minimum "cut-off" mark from 110 to 120. That the writ-petitioner submitted an application dated 2.01.2014 before the respondent No. 2 to consider the admission criteria of B.B.B.S. course as well as, to extend the deadline of the admission, pursuant to which the respondent No. 2 by memo being No. Sha: ODhi:/Chi: Shi:/Bibidho Bishoy. 2012/31 dated 07.01.2014 recommended that the minimum merit score for an applicant to be eligible for admission in M.B.B.S. course should be fixed at 105 instead for 120. The writ-petitioner submits that if the private medical/dental colleges are not allowed to admit students on the basis of the memo dated 04.12.2012 the concerned private medical colleges will suffer irreparable losses and injuries since 30% to 40% of the total seats in each private medical colleges would remain vacant. That the potential candidates also are approaching the writ-petitioner for redress of this situation.
